message.content:
For the expression  
\[
a(a-1)^{-1}\equiv 4a^{-1}\pmod{20}
\]
to make sense, both \(a\) and \(a-1\) must be invertible modulo \(20\). That means both must be relatively prime to \(20\).

But \(a\) and \(a-1\) are consecutive integers, so one of them is even. Since \(20\) is even, the even one shares a factor of \(2\) with \(20\), so it is not invertible modulo \(20\).

Thus, for every integer \(a\), at least one of \(a\) or \(a-1\) is not invertible modulo \(20\). Therefore the expression is never defined, so there are no solutions.

The answer is 0.
